cards.reason: The construction directly targets the short-return anomaly and a bounded choice of return procedure, with five-minute reconciliation and five complete kits as explicit outcome requirements. It preserves the five-minute loan, self-service return and one-tray inspection limit. Seventy-one accounted counters can supply five twelve-counter kits and an eleven-counter reserve remainder; the reserve is existing inventory, not an assumed purchase. Two volunteers, direct observation, separate counts, stopwatch and tally are available; no unavailable camera, extra block, staff or counters are indispensable. The hypothesized borrower-origin arrival before search separates H1 for a witnessed event from an other-source transfer or no-transfer recount. Persistent shortage, other-source recovery, unlogged repair and truncated observation have explicit consequences. O4 and O5 support the attribution problem, O7 the timing and observation gaps, and M1-M4 the proposed measurements. Historical origins and shared count errors remain unresolved. Five serviceable circulating kits is a plausible target, while simultaneous shelf readiness and actual outcome preservation are explicitly unproven; this uncertainty limits success claims without removing anchor fit.

The card addresses why short counts appear to recover and connects that account to a bounded return procedure, five complete kits, and a five-minute deadline. It preserves full loans, self-service return and twelve-counter issuance. Its sixty-second announcement gate uses the available two volunteers, stopwatch, tally, trays, mat and accounted inventory; it requires no unavailable indispensable resource. Sequential early eligible returns and explicit incomplete-follow-up reporting bound feasibility within the single block. Directly witnessed borrower arrival before announcement can reject shortage-triggered recovery for that event; a witnessed volunteer transfer after announcement identifies replenishment rather than borrower completion. A timing shift in only two events cannot establish a population causal effect, and the card explicitly retains demand, attention and background-traffic alternatives. No anomaly or missed origins yields an inconclusive comparison, while unresolved shortage at five minutes defeats reconciliation. P2 provides the report/search pathway, O4-O5 the apparent-recovery and origin problem, and M1-M4 the measurements. The report-trigger hypothesis is proposed, not asserted as observed, so source support is adequate at the stated exploratory claim ceiling.

The card targets short returns through a bounded own-tray comparison and explicitly carries the five-kit and five-minute outcome requirements into its defeat criteria. It distinguishes circulating inventory from simultaneously ready shelf kits and does not claim either interpretation has been achieved. Five complete kits plus eleven separately accounted counters fit the seventy-one-counter resource; further losses and replenishment remain conditional. The construction uses available direct watching, independent counts, the two volunteers and existing timing and tally materials, with one selected tray at a time and no loan interruption. Its source_refs mention R7 as the unavailable-resource boundary, but its indispensable resources are R1-R6; no camera, extra staff, new counters or second block is assumed. A witnessed corresponding-borrower arrival before search differs observably from an unrelated or volunteer transfer and from a no-transfer recount. Agreed unresolved shortage, inadequate kits under the stated interpretation, inspection overlap, missed origins and block truncation have explicit failure or inconclusive consequences. O3-O5 and O7 motivate the test, M1-M4 make it measurable, and U1-U3 delimit what remains unknown. Pressure and routing effects remain hypotheses rather than established causes.
